messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA Disease Model Help
parts:
On Tue, 2018-09-18 at 13:22 -0700, Oliver Stoner wrote:
>
> model <- Cases ~
> f(Region, model = "bym2", graph = 'graph.graph', constr = TRUE) +
> f(Week, model = "rw2", cyclic = TRUE, constr = TRUE) +
> f(Delay, model = "rw1", constr= TRUE, group = Region) +
> f(Time, model = "rw1", constr = TRUE,
> group = Region, control.group = list(model = 'iid'), replicate =
> Delay)


Hi Oliver,

can you try this model? I remove some default options. Its generally
advisable to scale these models, so I added that.

Make sure 'Delay' is 1, 2, 3, ... since you do replicate over it. I
would guess 'Region' is already 1,2,3,...



model <- Cases ~
f(Region, model = "bym2", graph = 'graph.graph') +
f(Week, model = "rw2", cyclic = TRUE, scale.model=T) +
f(Delay, model = "rw1", scale.model=TRUE, replicate= Region) +
f(Time, model = "rw1",
group = Region, control.group = list(model = 'iid'), replicate =
Delay)

I would guess the big cost comes from this term

f(Time, model = "rw1",
group = Region, control.group = list(model = 'iid'), replicate =
Delay)


you can try...


also, to improve speed, check out

inla.pardiso()



you can also try to reduce the dimension to improve speed, like using
26 weeks instead of 52, f.ex, and so on...


Let me know how this goes,

Best
H
